Two things were awkward. Neither blocked the task.

1. **The post-edit warning gave me no way to check it.** The hook said my edit "may invalidate memory 01a0fc13-5398 ('Invoice PDF rendering')". I didn't want to dismiss it without looking. The memory had no full ID, and the hook didn't say why it was flagged. I wanted a `get` that accepts the short ID prefix, and a field on the warning saying which path or `invalidated_by` glob matched. With those I could have confirmed the warning was a false positive, not just guessed. I also wanted a way to mark a memory as checked and unaffected without a full `verify` or `challenge`. I didn't try `get` on the short ID, so I don't know whether it would have resolved.

2. **Truncated previews had no way to tell me whether the rest mattered.** The hook previews for the refund-approval, PII and DB-pooler memories were cut off. I didn't need the full text for a type hint, so I didn't fetch them. I wanted a flag on each preview marking whether it was cut off and whether the hidden part contains a constraint. A parameter like `detail_level: "full"` on the hook's injected context would also have let me read the memories without a separate `get`.

Nothing else was missing.
